thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: runtime-backpressure spike detected on prod-runners. 95th pct queueing > 350ms for 3m, error-rate uplift on downstream (~4% 5xx). Paging on-call rotation: @jordan :rotating_light:

jordan: on it. grabbing logs + checking in-flight counts. initiating triage.

eva: last deploy uneventful, but we've had a batch of long-sequence requests from a partner test. suggest immediate live mitigation: reduce max_inflight from 16 -> 8 for frontend-pool, enable aggressive shedding for low-priority routes.

sam: confirmed customer-facing errors reported to CS: a handful of accounts seeing 502s and timeouts. examples from logs: `upstream_error: timeout after 12s` and spikes in `queue_length`.

maria: running runbook step 2 (runtime mitigation). will apply in this order: 1) lower max_inflight 2) turn on shedding 3) tighten per-tenant burst limits. posting commands now.

dev-sre-bot: ACTION: applying config change to runtime-controlplane (idempotent).

maria: ```bash
# reduce max in-flight on frontend pool
curl -s -X POST https://ops-api.internal/v1/runtime/config 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN' 
  -d '{"pool":"frontend","max_inflight":8}'
```

dev-sre-bot: OK: config accepted. rolling to 3/5 shards.

deploy-bot: Canary config rollout started for runtime-controlplane (canary: shard-03).

jordan: good. also flip on shedding for `experimental` and `low-priority` routes: set `shedding=aggressive` and `min_acceptance_prob=0.25` so we reject cheap/long requests first.

eva: let's also temporarily disable streaming responses for free tier to reduce open connections. small UX regression but saves many in-flight slots.

sam: notifying CS now with impacted customers list + mitigation plan.

cs-bot: Notified #customer-success: affected customers: [acme-inc, beta-co, int-analytics]. CS asked for ETA and whether to open support tickets.

maria: additionally tightening per-tenant quotas for non-critical orgs: `quota.default_per_minute -> 60` and bump timeout longer for in-flight eviction logic to prefer shedding over killing active requests.

jordan: can we do a temporary soft-rate-limit for anonymous/free traffic? something like `global_rate=0.7` to drop some background traffic.

eva: yes, traffic-shaper command below.

maria: ```bash
# set global shaping to 70% for free tier
opsctl traffic-shaper set --scope free-tier --rate 0.7 --reason "backpressure mitigation"
```

dev-sre-bot: OK: traffic-shaper applied.

jordan: watching dashboards now. please post 1-2 minute updates.

(2m later)

maria: metrics: queue P95 -> 180ms (down from 380ms), 5xx down to 1.6% (from 4.0%). in-flight per-shard avg decreased from 14 -> 7.

sam: CS: customers acknowledging fewer errors; some still seeing transient 502s. flagging high-priority account `acme-inc` for a manual quota bump if they keep hitting errors.

jordan: good. next steps: 1) keep mitigations for 20m, 2) run deeper root cause (investigate long sequence traffic + model path causing longer runtimes), 3) follow-up postmortem and permanent tuning of default `max_inflight`.

eva: we should also add a safety runbook change: when queue P95 > 300ms for 3m, automatically reduce max_inflight by 50% and enable shedding. prevents human lag.

maria: filed infra ticket INFRA-4492 to make that auto-action and a config UI entry.

ops-oncall: leaving handoff note for next oncall: mitigations applied: max_inflight=8 (frontend), shedding=aggressive (low-priority), free-tier shaping=0.7, streaming disabled for free-tier. watch: queue P95, 5xx, and per-tenant error bursts.

jordan: handing back to normal rotation. will convene postmortem in ~24h. thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity lowered to SEV-2. root cause investigation in progress. follow-up: postmortem assigned to @eva and @maria.

sam: filed customer communication draft in #customer-success-drafts. I'll post after approval.

maria: final note: we'll evaluate bumping the default `max_inflight` down to 10 across the fleet after RCA to reduce tail amplification risk.

jordan: closing thread from on-call perspective — re-open if regressions.
